newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Azeris, Armenians in worst fighting for years.
newsitem.headline: Azeris, Armenians in worst fighting for years.

text.p: Azerbaijan and Armenia accused each other on Wednesday of staging cross-border attacks over the past week in the worst fighting since the two countries signed a 1994 cease-fire.

Azerbaijan said it had killed or wounded at least 13 Armenian soldiers who had attacked its territory since Monday. Armenia called the charges a "fairy tale" designed to cover up Azeri battle losses over the week.

The Azeri Defence Ministry accused Armenian forces of staging forays into its territory along the northern part of the border between the two countries, while Armenia said the Azeris were the ones who had attacked.

Christian Armenians and Moslem Azeris went to war in the late 1980's over the region of Nagorno-Karabakh, an age old territorial dispute between the two. Before the war Karabakh was populated by Armenians, but it is inside Azerbaijan's borders.

The fighting, which subsided three years ago with the signing of the truce, killed thousands and was the first serious ethnic conflict in the former Soviet Union. Despite the cease-fire, no political solution has been found.

Azerbaijan's defence ministry said in a statement Armenian forces shelled and then attacked its troops on Monday in the Kazakh region, nearly 500 km (300 miles) north of the capital Baku. The statement said three Armenians had been killed.

The statement said 10 more Armenians were killed or hurt later on Monday after they tried to attack but ended up in a minefield. It said three more Armenians had been killed in fighting on Tuesday but reported no Azeri losses.
The statement said sporadic skirmishes were still going on in the area on Wednesday.

Armenian defence ministry spokesman Seiran Shakhsuvaryan confirmed clashes in the same area but said the Azeris were the ones who attacked. He called Baku's account of events a "fairy tale," and said that only one Armenian officer had been badly injured.
He said Armenian forces had killed seven Azeris on April 10 in fighting along the south of the tense frontier.
Shakhsuvaryan accused the Azeris of preparing for larger scale attacks along the border.
A vital oil pipeline runs within 35 kilometers (22 miles) of the area of the fighting along the Azeri side of the border.

A consortium of international petroleum giants plans to start using it in 1998 to export crude from its new $8 billion project in the Caspian Sea, the biggest of several deals Baku has secured up to develop its massive untapped reserves.
Shakhsuvaryan called the clashes the worst since the truce was signed three years ago and said the Azeris had staged 24 attacks since the beginning of April.
Armenian forces hold nearly 20 percent of Azeri territory, including Karabakh, which is legally Azerbaijan's but is populated by ethnic Armenians.
